title: Consolidate SLO alert groups and adjust burn sensitivity for capacity regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: After the Feb 6 capacity regression incident that triggered cascading burn-rate pages across multiple regions, we need a focused follow-up to reduce noisy pages while preserving rapid detection of true SLO breaches. This ticket consolidates alert groups, tunes burn-rate sensitivity for capacity-style regressions, and implements aggregation/debounce strategies to avoid flooding on transient upstream failures.

Goals:
- Prevent multi-route page floods for the same underlying capacity event.
- Ensure burn-rate alerts remain reliable for persistent degradations while not firing on short-lived spikes.
- Provide an automated simulation/test harness to validate thresholds against historical incidents.
- Roll out changes safely with canary windows and metric dashboards.

Scope of work (high level):
1) Alert group consolidation: group burn-rate alerts by service, region, and affected infra cluster rather than by route + model variant. Implement routing metadata in the alert payload to make aggregated decisions server-side.
2) Dynamic windowing: use an adaptive burn window that lengthens when correlated signals from multiple routes are present (to avoid immediate paging on fan-out failures), but shortens for single-route hard regressions.
3) Debounce & rate-limit paging: add a backoff policy that delays re-paging for the same incident context for N minutes, with aggressive lift for P0 customers.
4) Tier-aware thresholds: align burn-rate thresholds with customer tiers and SLAs; P0/P1 customers keep lower thresholds and faster paging, P2/P3 use queued notifications.
5) Simulation harness: replay Feb 6 event and a set of historical spikes with the new grouping/windowing logic to validate false-positive reduction and time-to-detect on true outages.
6) Dashboard + runbook updates: update Console SLO dashboard to show grouped burn attribution and add a runbook describing how to investigate grouped alerts and mute at the cluster level.

Deliverables:
- Alerting config PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-alerting/pull/274 (config + unit tests)
- Simulation harness: github.com/redwood-inference/slo-tests/pull/83 (replay scripts + sample datasets)
- Console dashboard: dashboards.redwood-inference.com/slo/grouped-burn (draft link)
- Runbook: confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Grouped+Alerting+Runbook

Trade-offs and notes:
- Grouping by cluster may delay detection for route-specific regressions; mitigated via tier-aware overrides and shorter windows for single-route anomalies.
- Dynamic windowing increases complexity in monitoring and requires careful observability to avoid masking slow regressions. We will instrument window length and matched event counts.
- Debounce/backoff reduces noise but can increase mean-time-to-detect for recurring short bursts; acceptable for non-P0 customers per product decision.

Acceptance criteria:
- 60% reduction in pager events on simulated Feb 6 replay without increasing median time-to-detect for P0 by more than 10% (measured in simulation).
- Config PR merged and deployed to staged alerting cluster with feature flag.
- Dashboard and runbook published and linked in the PR.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (staging): implement config and simulation, run against historical incidents (owners: Liam Chen, Kayla Morgan) -- 1 week.
- Phase 2 (canary): deploy grouping + windowing behind feature flag to 10% of clusters for non-P0 customers; monitor SLO time-to-detect and pager counts for 48 hours.
- Phase 3 (gradual): expand to all clusters for P2/P3 and 50% for P1 customers; keep P0 thresholds unchanged by default.
- Phase 4 (full): flip feature flag for all non-P0 and evaluate for P0 after stakeholder sign-off.

Stakeholders and reviewers:
- PM: Diego Rivera
- SRE: Kayla Morgan
- Product: Priya Desai
- On-call rotation: infra-oncall@redwood-inference.com

Notes from incident postmortem (Feb 6):
- Root cause: autoscaler misconfiguration + noisy throttling at the model-serving layer caused per-route latency spikes; burn-rate alerts fired independently for 14 routes across two regions.
- Problem: alerting topology caused each route to page different on-call teams, creating coordination overhead and delayed remediation.
- Recommendation: consolidate at cluster/service level and provide cross-route context in notifications.
